title: Get
about: Phrasal verbs and idioms with get: everyday ones like get by, get into and get together, and fixed expressions such as get down to business, get off someone's back and get away with murder.

parts.title: Getting down to a good gossip
Tip: one verb, many meanings
parts.note: Багато фразових дієслів мають цілий ряд значень. Якщо знайоме дієслово в реченні «не працює», перевір його в словнику, наприклад на dictionary.cambridge.org: можливо, тут інше значення. У таблиці — дієслова з get у значенні з цього юніту та в іншому поширеному значенні.

rows: get around
Word got around that the shop was closing.
We found a way to get around the parking rules.
get off
I get off at six on Fridays.
We get off at the next stop.
get in
Let's get a swim in before breakfast.
What time does your train get in?
get into
She's really got into yoga.
He got into a good university.
get down
The rain is getting me down.
Get down from that wall!
get by
We get by on one salary.
Excuse me, could I get by?
get up to
The kids are getting up to mischief.
We got up to page 50 last lesson.
get across
We need to get the message across.
How did you get across the river?

items.pattern: get my/your/his/her act together · informal · no object; the possessive matches the subject: She needs to get her act together.
items.meaning: start organising yourself and your life properly instead of being lazy or chaotic
items.example: If Max wants to pass his driving test, he'll have to **get his act together**.
more: The café was chaos at first, but the new owners soon **got their act together**.
I really need to **get my act together** and start saving for the summer.
items.watchOut: Присвійний займенник узгоджується з підметом: I get my act together, she gets her act together. Не «get the act together». Act тут — «поведінка, спосіб діяти», а не «акт». Розмовне.

items.pattern: news / word / a rumour gets around · no object · UK also get round
items.meaning: become known by more and more people as it is passed from person to person
items.example: In a small village, news **gets around** fast.
more: Word **got around** that the bakery was closing, and there was a queue all morning.
I don't know how it **got around**, but everyone at work knows I'm moving to Canada.
items.watchOut: Підмет — новина чи чутка: News gets around. Про людину get around означає «багато їздити» (див. частину C). Британською також get round.

items.pattern: no object · get by on a pension / on one salary / on £900 a month
items.meaning: have just enough money to pay for the things you really need, but no more
items.uk: зводити кінці з кінцями, якось перебиватися
items.example: After Dad retired, my parents had to **get by** on his pension.
more: Lots of students **get by** on pasta and cheap coffee.
We haven't got much, but we **get by**.
items.watchOut: Сума чи джерело доходу — після on: get by on a pension / on £900 a month. With — про те, що маєш, хоч цього й мало: get by with an old car, get by with basic English. Get by without sth — «обходитися без чогось»: We get by without a car.

items.pattern: sth gets sb down · the person goes between get and down: it gets me down (never gets down me) · often: Don't let it get you down.
items.meaning: make someone feel unhappy, tired of things or depressed
items.example: Commuting two hours a day was really **getting** him **down**.
more: Don't let one bad exam result **get you down**.
The constant noise from next door **got** her **down** in the end.
items.watchOut: Займенник — між get і down: it gets me down, а не it gets down me. Підмет — те, що пригнічує (погода, робота), а не людина, якій сумно.

items.pattern: no object · get off (work) at six / early · informal
items.meaning: finish work and leave for the day
items.example: I **get off** at six on Fridays, so let's meet at half past.
more: Could you **get off** work early and pick up the kids?
What time does your sister **get off** on Saturdays?
items.watchOut: «Звільнитися о шостій» (закінчити робочий день) — get off at six. Звільнитися з роботи назовсім — quit або leave a job. Get off ще означає «вийти з автобуса», тож часто додають work: get off work.

items.pattern: be getting up to mischief · get up to + mischief / no good · usually about children or pets, often in the continuous
items.meaning: do naughty things, usually in a playful rather than a serious way
items.example: It's far too quiet upstairs. I bet the twins are **getting up to mischief**.
more: Grandad says he **got up to** all kinds of **mischief** as a boy.
Keep an eye on the boys at the party – they'll **get up to mischief** if they're bored.
items.watchOut: Get up — «вставати», а get up to — «утнути, накоїти». Без to нічого не вийде: getting up mischief — помилка. У mischief наголос на перший склад.

items.pattern: no object · not separable · also get down to work / to sth / to doing sth
items.meaning: stop chatting and start dealing seriously with the thing you are there to do
items.example: The lawyer shook our hands, sat down and **got** straight **down to business**.
more: The new manager doesn't like small talk – she likes to **get down to business** at once.
After the holidays it took me a week to **get down to** some serious revision.
items.watchOut: «Перейти до справи» — не go to business. Після to — іменник або -ing: get down to work, get down to writing the report (не to write).

items.pattern: get off my/his/her back · informal, often an annoyed request: Get off my back!
items.meaning: stop criticising someone or telling them what to do all the time
items.example: Once I'd found a job, my parents finally **got off my back**.
more: Tell your coach you're injured – then maybe he'll **get off your back**.
My boss never **gets off my back** about being two minutes late.
items.watchOut: Розмовне й досить різке — не для листа незнайомій людині. Займенник змінюється: get off my/his/her back. Протилежне — be on sb's back: Mum's always on my back.

items.pattern: no object · also go back to basics
items.meaning: return to the simple, most important things after something has become too complicated
items.uk: повернутися до основ, до простих речей
items.example: After years of expensive gadgets, I've **got back to basics** with a paper diary and a pen.
more: The new head teacher wants the school to **get back to basics** – reading, writing and maths.
When the shop started losing money, the owners decided to **get back to basics** and sell only bread.
items.watchOut: Basics — завжди множина: back to basics, не back to the basic. Так само кажуть go back to basics.

items.pattern: a project / business / plan gets off the ground · get sth off the ground (start it successfully)
items.meaning: start happening or start working successfully (a plan, project or business)
items.uk: зрушити з місця, стати на ноги (про справу)
items.example: Our plan for a community garden finally **got off the ground** in the spring.
more: It took two years and a bank loan to **get** the bakery **off the ground**.
We need more volunteers to **get** the summer festival **off the ground**.
items.watchOut: Буквально — «відірватися від землі», як літак. «Зрушити з мертвої точки» не перекладай дослівно: кажуть the project finally got off the ground.

items.phrase: get sb/sth out of your mind
items.pattern: (can't) get sb/sth out of your mind / head · the object goes between get and out of: get it out of my mind · usually with can't
items.meaning: stop thinking about someone or something (usually said when you can't)
items.example: I can't **get** that sad film **out of my mind**.
more: She tried to **get** the argument **out of her mind** and go to sleep.
That song is so catchy – I can't **get it out of my head**.
items.watchOut: Об'єкт стоїть між get і out of: get it out of my mind. «Викинути з голови» — не throw out of my head. Обережно: be out of your mind — «з'їхати з глузду» (Are you out of your mind?).

items.pattern: get the message / your point across (to sb) · get across that… / how… · also put sth across
items.meaning: make people understand an idea or a piece of information
items.example: Our teacher used real stories to **get the message across** that smoking kills.
more: It's hard to **get** your **point across** when everyone's shouting.
Posters in every school **get across** how dangerous the river is in spring.
items.watchOut: «Донести думку» — не bring the message. Кажуть get (або put) the message across. Без across get the message означає «зрозуміти натяк»: OK, I get the message!

items.pattern: get away with murder · informal, an exaggeration · general: get away with sth / with doing sth
items.meaning: be allowed to behave badly again and again without being criticised or punished
items.example: My little brother **got away with murder** when we were kids – I always got the blame.
more: Our dog **gets away with murder** because he looks so sweet.
In my first job I noticed that the boss's favourites **got away with murder**.
items.watchOut: Murder тут — перебільшення: ніхто нікого не вбиває. Про одну конкретну провину — get away with sth: He got away with lying. Не плутай з get away from — «втекти від».

items.phrase: get to the bottom of sth
items.pattern: get to the bottom of a problem / a mystery / it · not separable
items.meaning: find out the real cause of something or the truth about it
items.uk: докопатися до суті, з'ясувати, у чому справа
items.example: Someone keeps taking my milk from the office fridge, and I'm going to **get to the bottom of** it.
more: Doctors still haven't **got to the bottom of** her headaches.
Police are trying to **get to the bottom of** what happened that night.
items.watchOut: Of обов'язковий: get to the bottom of the problem / of it. «Дійти до суті» — не reach the essence.

items.pattern: get in on the act · informal, often a little disapproving · also get in on sth (the fun, a deal)
items.meaning: start taking part in something that has become successful or popular, to get a share of the benefit
items.uk: і собі долучитися до вигідної справи
items.example: When one café on the street started selling bubble tea, the others soon **got in on the act**.
more: My little brother saw us baking and wanted to **get in on the act** too.
Now that padel is so popular, every sports shop wants to **get in on the act**.
items.watchOut: Дві частки поспіль, і обидві потрібні: in on. Часто з відтінком несхвалення: хтось хоче примазатися до чужого успіху.

items.pattern: What have you been getting up to? · get up to + much / a lot / anything · informal, often in friendly questions
items.meaning: do something, especially in your free time
items.example: So what have you been **getting up to** since you retired?
more: What did the kids **get up to** at summer camp?
My neighbour **gets up to** all sorts in her shed – pottery, woodwork, you name it.
items.watchOut: What have you been getting up to? — «Що поробляєш?», а What time do you get up? — «О котрій встаєш?». Одне to змінює все питання. Тут немає відтінку бешкету, як у get up to mischief.

items.pattern: sb gets around (a lot) · no object; + a place = move around it: get around the city by bus · UK also get round / get about
items.meaning: travel to lots of different places; also move from place to place
items.example: As a tour guide, Marta really **gets around** – she's in a different city every week.
more: Since Gran got her bus pass, she **gets around** much more.
You certainly **get around** – weren't you in Rome last month?
items.watchOut: Get around a lot — «багато їздити». Get around + місто — «пересуватися містом»: get around Lviv by tram (можна й get around in Lviv). Обережно: про людину без контексту (She really gets around) — це ще й натяк «має багато сексуальних партнерів», тож краще додати, куди саме людина їздить.

items.pattern: get into sth / doing sth · get really into sth · a hobby, music, a sport, a series
items.meaning: become interested in an activity or subject and start to enjoy it
items.example: I **got into** yoga during the long winter and now I do it every morning.
more: She **got into** photography after her trip to Iceland.
Lately my dad has **got into** old rock music, so the house is never quiet.
items.watchOut: «Захопитися чимось» — get into sth, без with: get into jazz, а не get into with jazz. Буквально get into — «залізти, потрапити»: get into a car, get into university.

items.pattern: get in sth / get sth in · separable: get in a swim, get a swim in, get it in (pronoun only in the middle)
items.meaning: manage to find time for an activity in a busy day
items.example: On holiday I always try to **get in** a bit of reading before the kids wake up.
more: We managed to **get** a game of cards **in** before the taxi came.
With two jobs, it's hard to **get** any exercise **in**.
items.watchOut: Частка може стояти до або після іменника: get in a swim = get a swim in. З займенником — лише get it in. Схоже значення має fit sth in.

items.pattern: get a lot / something / nothing out of sth · get sth out of a course, a trip, a book
items.meaning: get some benefit, enjoyment or value from something
items.example: I **got** a lot **out of** the first-aid course – I feel much more confident now.
more: My mum **gets** a lot **out of** her choir – it's the highlight of her week.
I didn't **get** much **out of** the lecture – it was far too technical.
items.watchOut: Що саме отримуєш — між get і out of: get a lot / nothing / something out of it. Потрібні обидві частки: out of, а не просто out.

items.pattern: get back into sth / doing sth · the routine, the habit of…, running, work
items.meaning: start doing an activity or routine again after a break
items.example: After three weeks in hospital, Dad is slowly **getting back into** his old routine.
more: I need to **get back into** the habit of cooking at home.
Once the exams were over, I finally **got back into** reading for fun.
items.watchOut: Get back into — знову втягнутися (у ритм, звичку, спорт). Не плутай з get back at sb — «помститися».

items.pattern: no object · get together (with sb) for a coffee / at sb's house · noun: a get-together
items.meaning: meet socially, usually in a relaxed way
items.example: Let's **get together** for a coffee when you're back from holiday.
more: The neighbours **get together** once a year to clean up the park.
We had a small **get-together** for Mum's birthday.
items.watchOut: Не meet together — просто meet або get together. Є й іменник a get-together — невелика зустріч чи вечірка.

warmup.q: This grey weather is really getting ___.
warmup.explain: Get sb down — пригнічувати. Займенник стоїть між get і down: it gets me down.

warmup.uk: Ми якось зводимо кінці з кінцями на одну зарплату.
warmup.explain: Get by — зводити кінці з кінцями. Ще кажуть make ends meet, а «з'єднувати кінці» — калька.

warmup.q: Let's stop gossiping and ___ to business.
warmup.explain: Перейти до справи — get down to business. Go to business і pass to business — кальки.

warmup.uk: Він ніяк не може викинути її з голови.
warmup.q: He just can't get her ___ his mind.
warmup.explain: Get sb out of your mind (або head) — викинути з голови.

warmup.uk: Батьки дозволяють йому все — йому все сходить з рук.
warmup.explain: Get away with murder — «усе сходить з рук». Murder тут — перебільшення, а руки в англійському виразі не згадуються.

warmup.uk: Чутки про нового сусіда розійшлися миттєво.
warmup.q: Rumours about our new neighbour ___ in no time.
warmup.explain: Новини й чутки розходяться — get around (британською ще get round). Go apart — калька.
Get up to — «поробляти». Без to — get up, «вставати».

warmup.uk: Важко донести до людей, що сміття треба сортувати.
warmup.q: It's hard to ___ the message across that rubbish needs sorting.
warmup.explain: Донести думку — get the message across. Bring the message — калька з «донести».

A.q: Tom's late every day. He really needs to get his ___ together.
A.explain: Get your act together — взятися за розум, навести лад у справах.

A.q: Don't tell anyone yet – you know how quickly news gets ___ in this office.
What time do you get ___ work on Fridays?
A.explain: Get off (work) — закінчити роботу на сьогодні.

B.q: We chatted for a while, then got down to ___.
B.explain: Get down to business — перейти до справи.

B.q: The plan sounded good, but it never got off the ___.
B.explain: Get off the ground — зрушити з місця, успішно стартувати.

B.q: Something odd is going on, and I want to get to the ___ of it.
B.explain: Get to the bottom of sth — докопатися до суті.

C.q: What have you been getting ___ to since we last met?
C.explain: Get up to sth — поробляти, займатися чимось.

C.q: After a holiday in Italy, my mum's ___ cooking pasta from scratch – she makes it every Sunday.
We should get ___ more often – it's been ages since we all had dinner.

example.title: Lunch with Mia
example.uk:
У суботу ми з моєю давньою подругою Мією нарешті зустрілися на обід. «Ну, що поробляєш?» — запитала вона. Я розповіла, що захопилася гончарством і зазвичай встигаю вибратися на заняття у вихідні.

У Мії рік був важчий. Робота в офісі її пригнічувала, а начальник постійно до неї чіплявся. «Мені треба було взятися за розум», — сказала вона. Тож вона звільнилася і тепер перебивається підробітками, поки її маленька пекарня стає на ноги.

«Чутки тут розходяться швидко», — засміялася вона. Її хліб на заквасці такий популярний, що супермаркет по сусідству теж хоче на цьому заробити. Я пішла з відчуттям, що той обід дав мені дуже багато.
example.en:
On Saturday my old friend Mia and I finally [[got together|c7]] for lunch. "So, what have you been [[getting up to|c1]]?" she asked. I told her I'd [[got into|c3]] pottery and usually managed to [[get in|c4]] a class at weekends.

Mia's year had been harder. Her office job was [[getting her down|a4]], and her boss never [[got off her back|b3]]. "I had to [[get my act together|a1]]," she said. So she left, and now she's [[getting by|a3]] on part-time work while her little bakery [[gets off the ground|b5]].

"Word [[gets around|a2]] fast here," she laughed. Her sourdough is so popular that the supermarket next door wants to [[get in on the act|b10]]. I left feeling I'd [[got a lot out of|c5]] that lunch.
